briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Relief in Reach: Michigan Operators Find Openings as Psychedelics Go Mainstream Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding real paths forward — new dispensary formats, an expanding city cap, and a supplier-cost-sharing playbook — even as the 24% wholesale tax reshapes the map. Nationally, momentum is undeniable: a federal court just upheld medical marijuana's Schedule III status, and the FDA's historic psychedelics hearing plus Compass Pathways' and Eli Lilly's moves signal 2027 could be the breakout year for legal psilocybin and MDMA-based therapies.

local.text: Muskegon dispensary-restaurant pushes format further — Fields Cannary, a Muskegon development, is targeting a fall opening for its retail cannabis dispensary, with a full-service restaurant to follow.

Menominee could add four new dispensaries — a pending petition drive could lead to four more dispensaries in the city, formally increasing the local cap from nine to 13 stores, with organizers saying they turned in more than enough signatures to get the measure on the November ballot.

U.P. chain Rize grows despite 24% tax — Rize, which operates three Upper Michigan locations, has managed to sustain growth by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers, splitting the tax burden rather than absorbing it alone.

Treasury softens the first-year tax bite — Treasury will waive penalties and interest for the first three quarters of 2026 if a business pays at least 75 percent of what it owes on the new 24% wholesale tax, giving operators room to adjust.

Gubernatorial hopeful vows to kill wholesale tax — Democratic candidate Chris Swanson came out strongly against the 24% cannabis tax and promised that, if elected, he would work to repeal it, saying it is "not fair and equitable" to a licensed industry.

national.text: Federal court upholds medical marijuana's Schedule III win — reclassification opponents filed a lawsuit to stop medical marijuana's change in schedule, but that challenge was rebuffed this week in federal court, when the D.C. Circuit court left the medical marijuana rescheduling order in effect.

FDA holds landmark hearing on psychedelic therapies — the FDA's September 14 hearing marked one of the most consequential regulatory moments for psychedelic-assisted therapy to date, and MAPS attended and plans to submit formal, written testimony on systems readiness, therapist training, and patient access.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin drug nears 2027 launch — management struck an upbeat tone on clinical progress and commercial readiness at the Deutsche Bank Healthcare Summit, noting the company has finished two Phase III trials with strong statistical results and is now in rolling review with the FDA.

Eli Lilly closes major psychedelics acquisition — the AtaiBeckley acquisition by Eli Lilly, approved by stockholders on September 8, 2026 and expected to close September 11, brings BPL-003, VLS-01, and EMP-01 under Lilly's development umbrella.

Optimi Health advances MDMA trial for veterans — Optimi Health announced plans to launch a Health Canada-authorized Phase 3 clinical trial in 2027 evaluating MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD in up to 100 veterans and frontline workers, funded partly by a $15 million public offering alongside its Nasdaq listing.
